rationale: Hebrews 4:4 (BSB) introduces its quotation with its own formula -- "For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner" -- and then quotes Genesis 2:2 almost verbatim: "And on the seventh day God rested from all His works." That introductory formula and near-verbatim wording are why the type is quotation rather than allusion, and why the label is explicit rather than inferred. The surrounding unit, Hebrews 4:1-11, builds an extended argument about a "Sabbath rest for the people of God" (4:9) on that one quoted clause; the wider range is included because the argument depends on the whole unit, not on 4:4 read in isolation, but the quotation itself anchors at 4:3-4.
